dhp1:1: Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, (their quality is) made by mind,
dhp1:3: if with a base mind one speaks or acts,
dhp1:5: through that suffering follows him like a wheel (follows) the ox’s foot.
dhp2:1: Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, (their quality is) made by mind,
dhp2:3: if with pure mind one speaks or acts,
dhp2:5: through that happiness follows him like a shadow which does not depart.
dhp3:1: “He abused me, he struck at me, he overcame me, he robbed me,”
dhp3:4: those who bear ill-will towards this their hatred is never appeased.
dhp4:1: “He abused me, he struck at me, he overcame me, he robbed me,”
dhp4:4: those who do not bear ill-will towards this their hatred is appeased.
dhp5:2: For not by hatred do hatreds cease at any time in this place,
dhp5:4: they only cease with non-hatred, this truth is (surely) eternal.
dhp6:1: The others do not understand that we should restrain ourselves here,
dhp6:3: but (for) those here who do understand, through that, (their) dissensions will cease.
dhp7:1: Living contemplating what is pleasant, uncontrolled in sense faculties,
dhp7:4: not knowing the limit in food, indolent, low in energy –
dhp7:6: Māra surely overthrows that one, like wind (overthrows) a weak tree.
dhp8:1: Living contemplating the unpleasant, well-controlled in sense faculties,
dhp8:3: and knowing the limit in food, faithful, with energy aroused –
dhp8:5: Māra does not overthrow that one, just as wind does not (overthrow) a mountain made of rock.
dhp9:2: The one who, while still impure, would wear the renunciant’s robe,
dhp9:4: unendowed with restraint and truth, is not worthy of the renunciant’s robe.
dhp10:1: The one who, steady in virtue, throws out (any) impurity,
dhp10:4: endowed with restraint and truth, is indeed worthy of the renunciant’s robe.
dhp11:2: Finding the essential in what is unessential, and seeing the unessential in what is essential,
dhp11:3: they do not understand what is essential, and resort to wrong intention.
dhp12:1: Knowing the essential in what is essential, and the unessential in what is unessential,
dhp12:3: they understand what is essential, and resort to right intention.
dhp13:1: Just as the rain penetrates a house with thatching that is poor,
dhp13:3: so passion penetrates a mind that is undeveloped.
dhp14:2: Just as rain does not penetrate a house with thatching that is good,
dhp14:3: so passion cannot penetrate a mind that is well-developed.
dhp15:1: Here he laments, after death he laments,
dhp15:2: the wicked one laments in both places,
dhp15:4: seeing the defilement of his own deeds.
dhp16:1: Here he rejoices, after death he rejoices,
dhp16:2: the meritorious one rejoices in both places,
dhp16:4: seeing the purity of his own deeds.
dhp17:1: Here he suffers, after death he suffers,
dhp17:2: the wicked one suffers in both places,
dhp17:3: he suffers, thinking: “I have done wickedness,”
dhp17:4: gone to a bad fate, he suffers much more.
dhp18:1: Here she is happy, after death she is happy,
dhp18:2: the righteous one is happy in both places,
dhp18:3: she is happy, thinking: “I have done merit,”
dhp18:4: gone to a good fate, she is happy much more.
dhp19:2: the heedless fellow, who does not do (what they say),
dhp19:3: like a cowboy counting other’s cattle,
dhp19:4: does not partake of the ascetic life.
dhp20:1: Even though reciting but few scriptures,
dhp20:2: but living righteously in accordance with Dhamma,
dhp20:5: that one, unattached here and hereafter,
dhp20:7: The Chapter about the Pairs, the First
